source_row.rationale: NCBI Bookshelf's current Open RN labor-and-delivery chapter defines precipitous labor as labor and delivery that are extremely rapid, usually less than 3 hours from the start of contractions to birth, so option A fits. Option B cannot be established from total labor duration because tachysystole is defined by contraction frequency over time. Option C is the opposite pattern: an arrest disorder requires absent cervical progress, not rapid dilation followed by birth. Option D is incorrect because multiparity may shorten labor but does not remove a sub-3-hour course from the precipitous-labor definition.

source_row.stem: A multiparous client gives birth 2 hours 45 minutes after regular contractions begin. Cervical dilation and fetal descent progress rapidly, but no contraction-frequency data are documented. Which labor pattern best describes this course?
